scope_basis: All material four-case architectural conclusions, targeted research qualifications, design implications, lineage limits, and explicit gaps. Excludes field prevalence, mechanism effectiveness, independent convergence, browser or GUI transfer, closed-production internals, and HTML presentation.

claim_text: All four reviewed cases place a model-directed choice loop inside programmed execution, state, integrity, and recovery envelopes, while differing materially in where those envelopes begin and what they accept as completion.
confidence: high for the four pins; no effectiveness, prevalence, universality, or independent-convergence claim.

notes: Model-directed tool continuation sits inside programmed state, scheduling, retry, and recovery.
Ordinary model-directed execution sits inside typed mediation, state, and recovery.
Embedded model work sits inside retry, replay, liveness, compaction, and delivery policy.
The classic CLI loop sits inside programmed recovery plus conditioned verification and optional goal judging.

claim_text: Harness control is distributed: models select local actions, while runtime code, operators, configuration, providers, extensions, and evaluators own different admission, authority, continuity, and acceptance decisions.
artifact_location: Finding 1: model-directed does not mean model-controlled
confidence: high for the four case boundaries; owner vocabulary remains extensible.

notes: Core, coding layer, extensions, operator, and model divide control.
SDK, caller, preset, plugins, workspace, and model divide control.
Core, operator, channel, provider, model, plugins, and evaluators divide control.
Runtime, operator, provider, adapters, extensions, evaluators, and model divide control.

claim_text: Durable state and model-visible context are different architectural objects in all four cases: information can remain stored while being absent, summarized, filtered, or replaced in the next model call.
confidence: high for the structural distinction; outcome effects of each projection remain unmeasured or indirect.

notes: Append-only tree state is projected into active branch and compaction-aware context.
Durable event state and active View are explicit layers; condensation depends on agent construction.
Canonical state, provider projection, memory, queues, and process-local state have different boundaries.
SQLite and memory state differ from cached prompt, request-local material, and compacted active history.
Reports compaction failure hypotheses and a counter-design under a different protocol.
Reports compaction latency and variability under different models and tasks.

claim_text: A model-proposed action, its authorized execution, the raw environment result, and the model-visible observation are distinct stages even when one function implements several of them.
artifact_location: Finding 3: the result is not yet the observation
confidence: high for symbolic tool paths; low for browser and GUI transfer and exact outcome effects.

notes: Validation, trusted hooks, execution, and bounded evidence are distinct decisions.
Typed calls, actions, mediation, execution, observations, events, and model messages are distinguishable.
Authority and canonical, provider-facing, and recovery representations differ.
Filtering, authorization, execution, transformation, spill handling, and observation insertion are distinct.

location: abstract, ACI design sections, and retained ablation evidence
abstract, ACI design sections, and retained ablation evidence

claim_text: Runtime integrity and operational recovery do not establish task correctness. All four ordinary paths can accept a model-authored completion, while stronger evidence-backed or independent task-success acceptance is absent, optional, configuration- or surface-conditioned, or external.
artifact_location: Finding 4: runtime integrity is not task acceptance
confidence: high for the inspected defaults and layers; judge accuracy and private acceptance systems remain unknown.

notes: Recovery exists while the ordinary path can accept model completion without an independent task-success gate.
Ordinary completion exists while critics and goal judging are optional.
Operational completion and delivery are distinct from optional or external semantic checking.
Conditioned same-agent evidence checking and an optional goal judge supply qualified counter-shapes.

claim_text: Existing research and production guidance favor reliable external or executable feedback over ungrounded intrinsic self-correction and distinguish active-run trajectories from outcome evaluation.
confidence: moderate transfer confidence; feedback source, observability, judge independence, and version affect applicability.

notes: Reports stronger support for reliable external feedback than ungrounded intrinsic correction in reviewed literature.

location: The structure of an evaluation; trajectory versus outcome; non-determinism guidance
The structure of an evaluation; trajectory versus outcome; non-determinism guidance

claim_text: “Available” and “default” are not interchangeable: critics, goal judges, delegation, containment, compaction, memory adaptation, and verification policies vary by entry point, activation state, operator configuration, and sometimes migration history.
confidence: high for the named cases and pins; every default claim requires its applicable population.

notes: Compaction, delegation, and containment claims depend on the coding-session path and extensions.

Compaction, verification, goals, adaptation, curation, delegation, and containment vary by surface and configuration population.

claim_text: Extension and policy-injection surfaces reassign control across multiple responsibilities rather than forming one self-contained harness module; in the inspected paths, installed extension code can sit inside the trusted execution boundary.

confidence: high as a four-case analytical pattern; third-party behavior remains deployment-specific.

notes: Extensions can alter prompt, tools, observations, state, rendering, delegation, and validated arguments.

Policies and hooks span model selection through tool execution, persistence, and delivery.
Middleware and plugins span requests, context, tools, verification, sessions, children, and gateway events.

claim_text: Operational observability and external outcome evaluation are separate contracts: traces, events, costs, tests, and replay can explain operation without establishing task success or mechanism effectiveness.
confidence: high for the distinction; private production evaluation remains unknowable.

notes: Events, sessions, usage, tests, and exports do not form a task-level evaluation harness.
Telemetry, tests, critics, goals, and external evaluation occupy distinct layers.
Runtime diagnostics differ from scenario packs and judged QA.
Trajectories, usage, cost, tracing, and batch output do not establish outcomes.
